StatDef.label: extraction labor
StatDef.description:
Labor spent at the point of extraction — mining, harvesting, and butchery — to obtain the raw materials embodied in this thing, per unit.

Measured following the cheapest chain of production that could yield this thing. Nature contributes nothing: an ore vein's labor content is the work of mining it, not what the ore is worth.

Shown in every unit that says something, from the coarsest down to raw ticks: in-game hours of work (2,500 ticks each), work-seconds (60 ticks each, the unit a recipe's work amount is quoted in), and ticks. Small things read in ticks alone, because at that magnitude the coarser units are all zeroes.

StatDef.label: fabrication labor
StatDef.description:
Labor spent transforming materials into this thing — crafting, smithing, cooking, construction — summed over every production step, per unit.

Excludes the extraction labor embodied in the inputs, which is reported separately.

RimWorld's own pricing pays several times more for extraction labor than for fabrication labor, so a thing dominated by this stat is one whose labor the economy barely rewards.

Shown in every unit that says something, from the coarsest down to raw ticks: in-game hours of work (2,500 ticks each), work-seconds (60 ticks each, the unit a recipe's work amount is quoted in), and ticks. Small things read in ticks alone, because at that magnitude the coarser units are all zeroes.
